name: The Permit Process: A Step-by-Step Guide for Homeowners
description: The Permit Process: A Step-by-Step Guide for Homeowners

step.name: Step 1
step.text: Embarking on a renovation project in the Denver area often means navigating the permit process. Here’s a simple step-by-step guide to help you understand what's involved.

step.name: Step 2
step.text: **Step 1: Confirm Your Project Scope and Permit Type.** Before you even pick up a hammer, figure out exactly what you're doing. Is it a kitchen remodel, a basement finish, or something structural? This will determine if you need a permit and what kind. Different projects trigger different permits, especially if you're touching electrical, plumbing, or load-bearing walls. Don't treat major interior work as just cosmetic; it often isn't.

step.name: Step 3
step.text: **Step 2: Assemble Your Documents.** This is where you gather all your plans, calculations, and any supporting documents. Think architectural drawings, engineering reports, and product approvals. Incomplete documentation is a major cause of delays, so be thorough. Ensure everything clearly outlines your project.

step.name: Step 4
step.text: **Step 3: Submit Your Application and Pay Fees.** Once your package is complete, submit it to your local authority having jurisdiction (AHJ) – this could be your city or county. Be prepared to pay any associated fees at this stage. Some jurisdictions allow online submissions, while others require in-person drops.

step.name: Step 5
step.text: **Step 4: Schedule Inspections.** Once your permit is issued, you'll need to schedule inspections as work progresses. Many jurisdictions require inspections to be scheduled in advance, often a day or two before. Don't assume same-day requests are accepted. Coordinate with your contractor to ensure the site is ready and accessible for the inspector.

step.name: Step 6
step.text: **Step 5: Prepare for the Inspector.** On inspection day, make sure all relevant documents are on-site and easily accessible. The work being inspected should be ready, and any necessary tools or access equipment should be available. It's crucial not to cover up work, like closing walls, before it's been inspected and approved. Completing these steps correctly helps ensure your project stays compliant and on schedule.
